title: Modern surgery: anaesthesia and antisepsis
summary: On 16 October 1846 the dentist William Morton gave ether to a patient for a tumour operation by the surgeon John Collins Warren in the Ether Dome of Massachusetts General Hospital in Boston, showing that surgery could be painless. In Glasgow in the 1860s, Joseph Lister, drawing on Pasteur's work, used carbolic acid to kill germs in wounds and published his results in The Lancet in 1867. Together, anaesthesia and antisepsis let surgeons attempt complex operations with far lower death rates.

uncertainty.note: Morton demonstrated surgical ether anaesthesia on 16 October 1846; Lister published his landmark series on antiseptic surgery in The Lancet in 1867.
